summary: Re-verified all five findings against the current tree BEFORE editing: NONE was already fixed and none was wrong. src/sig/api.py and src/sig/levers.py are the only files I touched. THE HIGH ONE IS CLOSED: src/sig/api.py::_stop_verdict now takes a one-point curve -- the ABSOLUTE collapse arm (sep < 0.15) is a statement about ONE probe, the flatness test is the arm that needs a predecessor, and holding both behind `len(curve) < 2` is what made the RUN-LEVEL FAILURE verdict unproducible at the shipped SIG_WARMUP=800 / SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=500. Measured before: a stream on which every window is identical warmed to separation_final = -0.000000 and returned verdict='budget'. Measured after: verdict='collapsing' at step 500 with probes=1, counter sig.warmup_verdict='collapsing'. The gate's reason sentence that asserted this was already possible is no longer a promise: the arm now computes `collapse_points` (every probe at or after the floor, as against stop_points which starts at the second probe) and prints one of two clauses -- 'a collapse CAN be declared here' with the probe steps that make it true, or 'WHAT IS NOT LIVE EITHER ... sig.warmup_separation_final is the only surface that can show a collapse here' when no probe reaches the floor. Both clauses exercised. THE MEDIUM ONE IS CLOSED: the two setdefault calls that seeded sig.cadence_dense / sig.cadence_idle moved out of the ELSE of `if due:` to above the branch, so both keys exist from the first check on every arm; at the shipped SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=1, 50 dense windows now leave {'sig.cadence_checks': 50, 'sig.cadence_dense': 50, 'sig.cadence_idle': 0} where st.counters['sig.cadence_idle'] used to raise KeyError, and the idle-only, SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=2 and bigram runs that already seeded both keys are unchanged. THE THREE LOW ONES: (3) the `floor >= budget` gate reason now says the boundary is AT OR ABOVE SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC=1.0 and names the off-by-one it replaces -- verified UNREACHABLE at 1.0 and 1.01, reachable again at 0.99 -- and the unguarded NEGATIVE fraction is now a refusal at the one site that multiplies the fraction by the budget, beside the existing SIG_WARMUP and SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY refusals, because spine/lever.py::Lever carries choices and no numeric range; 0.0 still runs and still fires the stop. (4) the `period < 1` refusal now stands BELOW the `mode != 'learned'` early return, so SIG_MODE=bigram + SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=0 returns due=False under the gate that calls those levers inert instead of taking the run down for a modulo that arm never evaluates; the refusal keeps full force on the learned arm, verified on both the dense arm (SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=0) and the idle arm (wire = 0). (5) behaviour deliberately UNCHANGED -- WarmupReport still returns 'budget' with steps=0 on the bigram and SIG_WARMUP=0 arms -- and the CLAIM corrected instead: the docstring now defines 'budget' as the ABSENCE of a stop, names the two counters and the gate that separate a spent budget from an inert one, and records that a fourth verdict is a record-type change and the owner's ruling to make. Two overreaching claims in the same family were corrected where the tree states them: the 'UNREPRESENTABLE' sentence in warm_up's docstring, its floor comment and src/sig/levers.py's warmup_min_frac block now say the inverted pair is impossible STRICTLY BELOW 1.0 and reported from 1.0 up; src/sig/levers.py::SIGLevers.warmup_probe_every now records what the shipped 500-against-800 pair actually buys (one probe: no plateau stop, collapse alarm only). NO WIRE WAS SPENT, no lever was added or removed, no LEVERS READ / WIRES READ / DID IT FIRE name changed, no RNG stream was minted, and the five SIG entry points that were NotImplementedError stubs (train_step, counters, state_dict, load_state_dict, encoder_embedding) still are. Suite green after.

findings.detail: STILL PRESENT in the current tree when I started -- not already fixed -- and now FIXED. Re-verified first: `if t < floor or len(curve) < 2: continue` stood directly above the only call to src/sig/api.py::_stop_verdict, and the verifier's own script reproduced verdict='budget' at separation_final=-0.000000. THE FIX, three edits, no wire, no lever, no new surface: (a) src/sig/api.py::_stop_verdict now unpacks `sep, peak = curve[-1], max(curve)`, runs BOTH collapse arms, and returns None for want of a predecessor only when len(curve) < 2, taking `prev` after that guard -- for any curve of two or more points it is expression-for-expression the function it was, so nothing that already worked can move; (b) the loop's guard is now `if t < floor: continue`, i.e. the FLOOR still holds a verdict back and the probe COUNT no longer does; (c) the gate arm that asserted the collapse was still live now computes it: `collapse_points = tuple(t for t in grid if t >= floor)` beside the existing `stop_points`, and the reason prints the true clause of two. MEASURED AFTER, at the shipped defaults on the same all-identical stream: verdict='collapsing', steps=500, probes=1, separation_final=-0.000000, st.counters['sig.warmup_verdict']='collapsing', and the gate reason ends '...the probe(s) at step(s) [500] are at or after the floor -- so a collapse CAN be declared here and sig.warmup_verdict is the surface that says so'. NEIGHBOURS, all run: the same stream at SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=200 still returns 'collapsing' (now at step 200, the first probe at or after the floor of 200, rather than step 400 -- the same verdict, declared as soon as the floor allows); a HEALTHY random stream at the defaults returns 'budget' with separation 0.972994 and is NOT called collapsing; the same healthy stream at SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=100 still returns 'plateau' at step 300 with Gate sig.adaptive_stop FIRED and reachable=True, and at SIG_WARMUP=400 / probe 100 also FIRED -- so the gate made unreachable at the shipped cadence is still reachable everywhere the plateau mechanism can fire. The earliest a collapse can now be declared is the first probe AT OR AFTER int(SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC * SIG_WARMUP), which at defaults is 25% into the budget: a healthy encoder measured 0.97 there against the 0.15 threshold, and the run with SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC=0.0 and probes every 100 steps still reached 'plateau' rather than a false collapse.

findings.detail: BOTH HALVES RE-VERIFIED AS REAL and both fixed. (a) THE BOUNDARY: the arm is selected by `elif floor >= budget`, so at SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC=1.0 exactly, floor == budget and the gate is already UNREACHABLE -- confirmed again in this tree, 'Gate sig.adaptive_stop: UNREACHABLE (800 vs 800)' -- while the reason ended 'reachable again only above SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC=1.0', which sends a reader to the one value that does not work. The sentence now reads 'reachable again AT OR ABOVE SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC=1.0 -- at exactly 1.0 the floor IS the budget, this arm is the one selected, and a reader who followed an earlier wording of this sentence to 1.0 to get the stop back would have found it still unreachable. Below 1.0 the floor lands inside the budget and the stop can fire again.' Verified UNREACHABLE at 1.0 (400 vs 400) and 1.01 (404 vs 400), and reachable at 0.99 (396 vs 400). (b) THE NEGATIVE FRACTION: spine/lever.py::Lever carries `choices` and no numeric range, so units.FRACTION is a label; a negative fraction gave a negative floor, `t >= floor` true at the first probe, and no gate arm saying so -- every one of them reports a floor that is merely low. warm_up now refuses it at the one site that multiplies the fraction by the budget, beside the SIG_WARMUP and SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY refusals it already carried: 'SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC=-0.5: the floor is a SHARE of SIG_WARMUP=400 and a share cannot be negative. It would put the floor at -200 step(s), which no step count is below, so the adaptive stop would be eligible from the first probe onward -- the guard removed rather than lowered, and reported by no gate.' NEIGHBOUR: 0.0 is a legal fraction (no floor asked for) and still runs -- verdict 'plateau' at 300 steps with Gate sig.adaptive_stop FIRED (0 vs 400). THE CLAIM ITSELF was corrected in three places, because the same overreach was written down three times: warm_up's docstring and its floor comment said the inverted pair was UNREPRESENTABLE while this function's own gate arm for it stood below, and src/sig/levers.py::SIGLevers.warmup_min_frac said 'a fraction of the budget cannot exceed the budget'. All three now say the shape is impossible STRICTLY BELOW 1.0 and reported from 1.0 up, and name the negative end as refused rather than unrepresentable. NOT MINE TO EDIT: .rework/CENSUS.md carries the same 'not merely detected but unrepresentable' sentence in the ENC_WARMUP_MIN row -- the owner's ledger, reported not touched.

The gate's reason gained one clause saying why an incoherent cadence is not refused there either: 'this arm never divides by it.' DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, and reported rather than done quietly: sub-note (a), moving the refusal to build time. src/sig/api.py::build reads mode, space, d, bigram_dim and positive_radius_windows and neither the cadence levers nor the d_idle_cadence wire; relocating the check would add both to build's LEVERS READ / WIRES READ blocks and move a wire read to a second entry point to buy a startup refusal for a value the loop refuses on its first window. That is an owner's call about where SIG refuses, not a repair, and it is left undone. Sub-note (b) was already true and still is: the message renders both the message-only lever read (SIG_TRAIN_EVERY_IDLE) and the wire value.
